svg.title: The Daily Nexus system architecture
svg.desc: Operator-controlled inputs feed a Python generation runtime that runs either on a Windows desktop or on an ephemeral Linux runner. The runtime collects and sanitizes evidence, calls Antigravity for editorial work, then applies quality gates whose approved output feeds two separate renderers: Kokoro and FFmpeg for audio, and ReportLab and PyMuPDF for the newspaper. All state stays in private local storage: SQLite, episode files, and the operating-system credential vault. An optional per-operator private deployment adds a Cloudflare timing-only clock that wakes a private GitHub Actions runner, an owner-locked Firestore queue the runner reads and writes, and Firebase Hosting that the runner publishes to.
svg.text: WINDOWS DESKTOP, OR AN EPHEMERAL LINUX RUNNER
local speech, one pass per host
Approved output feeds both renderers; the spoken script is never reused as newspaper copy.
PRIVATE LOCAL STATE — NEVER COMMITTED, NEVER SENT TO A THIRD PARTY
OPTIONAL — ONE PRIVATE DEPLOYMENT PER OPERATOR
publishes, then re-verifies the live feed
Only a due schedule or an explicit request wakes the runner. It reads and writes the owner-only queue, runs the same runtime shown above, then publishes.
